description: We are a team of passionate university students interested in technology, programming, innovation, and space exploration. With backgrounds in computer science, coding, research, and creative problem-solving, we aim to turn real-world challenges into practical solutions. We welcome enthusiastic teammates with skills in web development, UI/UX design, data analysis, AI/ML, astronomy, and scientific research who enjoy collaboration and learning.
summary:
SpaceEcho is an interactive website that explores the stories of space equipment left behind by missions to the Moon, Mars and other parts of our solar system. The idea is to help people understand what these objects are, why they were sent into space and what they helped us discover.

Users can explore different destinations, click on mission markers and read about the equipment and missions. The website includes stories about Apollo, Surveyor, the Mars rovers, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer and Kepler.

It also includes a section based on NASA's Apollo Passive Seismic Experiment data, where users can explore event records, charts and information about seismic activity on the Moon.

We created SpaceEcho to make space exploration history easier and more interesting to learn about, especially for young students and people who are curious about space.
details:
How the project works

SpaceEcho is an interactive educational archive that tells the stories of space equipment and missions across the Moon, Mars and beyond. Visitors can choose a destination, explore its illustrated view, zoom and pan around it, and select mission markers to open individual story panels.

Each panel explains the mission, the equipment involved, why it was sent, its current status and the scientific work it contributed to. Photographs and source references are included to help visitors explore the missions further.

The Moon section covers Apollo equipment, ALSEP, Surveyor 3 and the Lunar Roving Vehicles. The Mars section features Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, Phoenix, InSight and Ingenuity. The Beyond section includes Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10 and 11, and the Kepler Space Telescope.

Scientific data

An additional feature explores the Apollo Passive Seismic Experiment Expanded Event Catalog from NASA's Planetary Data System. It presents the catalogue through data summaries, charts, a browsable event table and a lunar location visualization. This helps visitors understand how scientific instruments left on the Moon continued to provide valuable observations.

Benefits and intended impact

SpaceEcho makes space exploration history easier to discover by connecting hardware, mission stories, photographs and scientific data in one place. It is designed for school-age learners, including children and teenagers, as well as casual space enthusiasts of all ages.

The main goal is to encourage curiosity about space science and help visitors understand that the scientific value of a mission can continue long after its spacecraft stops operating.

Technology and development

The project was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with JSON and CSV files for storing and presenting information. It runs as a browser-based static web application and does not require a backend server or database.

Creativity and design considerations

The main creative idea is to turn a technical archive into an interactive exploration experience. Instead of reading a long list of mission records, visitors can explore destinations and discover individual stories at their own pace.

During development, we considered accessibility, simple explanations, navigation, visual clarity, source attribution and scientific accuracy. We also distinguish actual NASA photographs from artist concepts, models and AI-generated illustrations.

The Moon and Mars overview globes and selected Beyond illustrations are AI-generated visual aids, not NASA photographs or scientific basemaps. Mission markers are illustrative navigation points, not precise map coordinates. Published coordinates are included in mission details where available.

SpaceEcho is an independent educational project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA.
